claim.quote: The TeV image shows at least one new source MGRO J2019+37 as well as correlations with the matter density in the region as would be expected from cosmic-ray proton interactions.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal reference as printed on the arXiv page: Astrophys.J.658:L33-L36,2007.

key_value_text.quote: the TeV gamma-ray flux as measured at ~12 TeV from the Cygnus region (after excluding MGRO J2019+37) exceeds that predicted from a conventional model of cosmic ray production and propagation
key_value_text.value: TeV flux at about 12 TeV from the Cygnus region (after excluding MGRO J2019+37) exceeds that predicted by a conventional model of cosmic-ray production and propagation

name: Milagro discovers TeV gamma-ray emission from the Cygnus region

significance.note: The abstract states no significance; the figure is taken from the body of the paper.
significance.quote: This new source, MGRO J2019+37, is observed with a statistical significance ~ 6 standard deviations above the average diffuse gamma-ray emission in the region.
significance.value: MGRO J2019+37: about 6 standard deviations above the average diffuse emission in the region (Cygnus region excess: 10.9 standard deviations)

summary.plain: Milagro mapped TeV gamma rays from the Cygnus region of the Galaxy and found a new source, MGRO J2019+37. The gamma-ray flux from the region was brighter than a conventional model of cosmic rays predicts.
summary.technical: Spatial and flux measurements of TeV gamma-ray emission from the Cygnus Region: one new source MGRO J2019+37 and correlation with the matter density; the flux at about 12 TeV (excluding MGRO J2019+37) exceeds a conventional cosmic-ray production and propagation prediction.

title: Discovery of TeV Gamma-Ray Emission from the Cygnus Region of the Galaxy
why_it_matters: The abstract says the excess indicates hard-spectrum cosmic-ray sources and/or other TeV gamma-ray sources in the region.
